source.version: Journal version of record, Journal of Creativity 33 (2023) 100066, available online 9 October 2023 (Essex repository PDF, 7 pages); all numbers checked against the PDF pages
source.title_on_document: Artificial muses: Generative artificial intelligence chatbots have risen to human-level creativity

supplement.where: Online version at doi:10.1016/j.yjoc.2023.100066 (p. 6, Supplementary materials); data and R code at https://osf.io/9fctd/?view_only=6c8f02c6972b49319c12f87cfb3f76db (p. 1 footnote; p. 3)
supplement.holds: Table S1 (intraclass correlations by prompt), Figs. S1 and S2 (originality plots), and the fluency results (Figs. S3 and S4), which the main text only summarizes

paper_design_summary: 100 Prolific participants (native English speakers from the USA) completed the Alternative Uses Test for five objects without AI, and five generative AI chatbots (alpa.ai, Copy.ai, ChatGPT GPT-3, Studio, YouChat) answered the same five prompts; GPT-4 was added later in a follow-up. Six human raters (blind to the source) and a trained AI scoring model rated the originality of responses from the human participants and the five original chatbots; GPT-4 follow-up responses were rated only by the AI scorer (p. 3, Procedure and Results, GPT-4). No participant used AI (pp. 2-3, Method).

studies.label: Alternative Uses Test: 100 humans vs five (six with GPT-4) chatbots

assignment.what_was_assigned: No people were assigned to AI assistance; humans and chatbots generated separate AUT responses. Randomization concerned object-prompt order and the presentation of prompts and responses to raters.
assignment.quote: The order in which the prompts were presented was randomized.
assignment.locator: pp. 2-3, Method, Participants and chatbots; p. 3, Materials and Procedure

participants.who: Prolific participants, native English speakers from the USA with full- or part-time work (M age = 41.00, SD = 12.25, 50 women, 50 men); they wrote AUT ideas without AI. Separately, six human raters scored originality.
participants.quote: In total, 100 participants completed our study (Mage = 41.00, SD = 12.25, 50 women, 50 men), who were recruited through Prolific Academic.

ai_tool.name_model: alpa.ai, Copy.ai, ChatGPT (GPT-3), AI21 Studio (Jurassic-1), YouChat; ChatGPT GPT-4 added in a follow-up analysis
ai_tool.how_used: The chatbots produced AUT answers themselves with the prompt "What can you do with [prompt]?", one chat session per prompt, asked "What else?" up to three times (Copy.ai: "more like this"). No participant used AI.

task.description: Alternative Uses Test for five objects: ball, fork, pants, tire, toothbrush; humans listed as many uses as possible; prompt order randomized
task.duration: Three minutes per object for humans; average completion time 17 min (p. 2-3)

outcomes.name: Originality rated by six human raters
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Six human raters, blind to source, rated originality on a 1-5 scale (CAT method); ICCs 0.85-0.94; scores averaged per creator and prompt; linear mixed model with random intercepts and slopes for prompt; per-prompt between-subject t-tests in Table 1. GPT-4 was not rated by humans.

contrasts.treatment_arm: Five GAI chatbots (alpa.ai, Copy.ai, ChatGPT GPT-3, Studio, YouChat)

outcomes.name: Originality rated by a trained AI scoring model
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: LLM trained for AUT scoring (Organisciak et al., 2023); correlation with averaged human ratings rs = 0.78-0.94; same mixed model and per-prompt t-tests as S1-O1.

contrasts.treatment_arm: Five GAI chatbots (alpa.ai, Copy.ai, ChatGPT GPT-3, Studio, YouChat)

outcomes.name: Number of humans scoring above the most original chatbot (human ratings)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of the 100 human participants whose originality score from the six human raters exceeds the best original chatbot's score, by prompt (p. 4, Table 1, HumanR and H > GAI columns). GPT-4 was not rated by humans (p. 3, Results, GPT-4).

contrasts.treatment_arm: Most original GAI chatbot among the five original chatbots
contrasts.reported: Five original chatbots: H > GAI, HumanR: Pants 42, Ball 26, Tire 7, Fork 43, Tooth-brush 39.
contrasts.locator: p. 3, Results, Originality; p. 4, Table 1, HumanR and H > GAI columns

outcomes.name: Fluency (number of ideas)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Sum of ideas per participant or chatbot, counted by the six raters and the AI (no-answers excluded); results reported in the supplement only. Chatbots were prompted up to three extra times, so counts are not directly comparable (p. 5).

contrasts.reported: "Since most of the GAI chatbots were prompted multiple times, the GAI chatbots came up with 2-3 times more ideas than humans (Figs. S3, S4)." Fluency and originality: rs = -0.28 to 0.26.
contrasts.locator: p. 4, Results, Fluency (details in supplement Figs. S3, S4)

outcomes.name: Number of humans scoring above the most original chatbot (AI ratings)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of the 100 human participants whose originality score from the trained AI scorer exceeds the best original chatbot's score, by prompt (p. 4, Table 1, AIR and H > GAI columns). The GPT-4 follow-up uses AI ratings only (pp. 3-4, Results, GPT-4).

contrasts.treatment_arm: Most original GAI chatbot (five chatbots; GPT-4 in follow-up)
contrasts.reported: Five original chatbots: H > GAI, AIR: Pants 52, Ball 29, Tire 1, Fork 24, Tooth-brush 65. GPT-4 (AI-rated): 2 (pants), 29 (ball), none (tire), 3 (fork), 13 (toothbrush); "On average, 9.4 humans were more creative than ChatGPT version 4 across all prompts."
contrasts.locator: p. 4, Table 1, AIR and H > GAI columns; pp. 3-4, Results, GPT-4

eligibility.reason: This compares chatbot-generated AUT answers with separately generated answers from 100 human participants; no person was assigned to or received AI assistance (pp. 2-3, Method, Participants and chatbots and Materials). The 100 human completers meet the people-count criterion (p. 2, Participants and chatbots), and originality and fluency were scored on their output (p. 3, Procedure and Results). The study therefore qualifies as AI-versus-human context evidence, outside the core dataset.

one_line_finding: Mixed models found no mean difference in Alternative Uses originality between 100 humans and five chatbots, whether rated by six humans (B = -0.21, SE = 0.15, p = .218) or by an AI scorer (B = -0.18, SE = 0.13, p = .241) (p. 3; per-prompt t-tests in Table 1, p. 4), and on average 9.4 humans scored above GPT-4 (p. 4).
notes: The Results section also reports "Across all prompts, 32.8 humans were more original than the most original GAI." (p. 3, Results, Originality), without identifying a specific rating method for this across-prompt summary.

Six human raters (blind to the source) and a trained AI scoring model rated the originality of every response, and the paper compares human and chatbot scores. No participant used AI.
